data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 proposes an abstraction relation but names no causal mechanism by which the shared environmental variables produce the non-Poisson failure pattern. The 'refuted if' clause references the observational outcome (Poisson distribution) but the substantive claim—the dependence of telemetry requirements on cross-domain temporal correlation—lacks any stated mechanism connecting the environmental variables to failure correlation. Without specifying whether the shared variables influence failure rates directly, mediate common-mode triggers, or modulate detection latency, the abstraction is a relabeling of a statistical observation, not a substantive dependence relation. A genuine abstraction would identify what causal feature of SRC_003's telemetry is being generalized—e.g., that common environmental drivers induce correlated failure times across domains—instead of merely asserting that the principle exists and is falsified by a particular distribution.
